ESEN

Anthropologist · researcher · educator

I investigate how we construct partial ways of knowing and intervening in the world.

My work articulates ethnography, pedagogy and material experimentation to examine how experiences, organisms and environments are translated into categories, data, instruments and forms of action. I am currently developing a doctoral ethnography in plant biotechnology laboratories in Chile.

an operation

I am currently investigating how plant life comes to acquire coherence as a scientific object.

I am developing an ethnography in plant biotechnology laboratories in Chile. The research follows the operations through which living organisms are extracted from their contexts, fragmented and transformed into samples, sequences, databases and other forms of information that allow them to be compared, circulated and intervened.

Research in progress · Ph.D.

Making life coherent

An ethnography in plant biotechnology laboratories in Chile.

Biotechnology does not work with a completely stable or controllable life. To produce knowledge and intervene in living organisms, materials, techniques, biological rhythms, experiments, institutions and future expectations must be temporarily coordinated. My research examines how these coordinations are built, how they are sustained, and what happens when they are interrupted or overwhelmed.

Question

What happens to plant life when it is translated into genetic information and how do the material, temporal and institutional operations that make this translation possible produce and stress its coherence as a scientific object?

Subject and information

How organisms, tissues and samples become comparable and circulatable data.

Temporalities and coherence

How biological, experimental and institutional rhythms are coordinated without completely coinciding.

Promises and institutions

How drought, innovation and the future guide investments, scientific priorities and forms of intervention.

Design conditions to learn by doing and think with others

My pedagogical practice has developed through the construction of materials, work sequences and forms of accompaniment. I am interested in teaching as a mediation practice that allows one to gradually approach complex problems, rehearse ways of approaching them, and review what occurs with others.

The cases gathered here show three scales of this work: converting several years of teaching into a reusable guide, accompanying students during the formulation of their research projects, and organizing an applied experience in collaboration with an organization.

Completed manuscript · 2024 · Under editorial contract

Pedagogical guide to social sciences

Build a value chain through applied research

Two students developed a diagnosis on the value chain of shrimp and prawn fishing together with the Association of Fisheries Industrialists and Shipowners of Coquimbo. The work combined documentary review, interviews, data analysis and iterative construction of a diagram.

My contribution

I designed the assignment, managed the initial link, accompanied the field work and analysis, proposed using the value chain model and guided the successive versions of the diagram prepared by the students.

Three formations, one sedimentation path

My career brings together psychology, sociology and anthropology as part of a deliberate search to expand the scales from which to understand knowledge and action. From my initial training I wanted to move towards sociology and anthropology because I found excessively individualizing explanations insufficient. Sociology allowed me to study policies, institutions and government devices; Anthropology later emerged as a way to get closer to specific practices that the institutional analysis of my master's thesis could not observe.

This direction existed from early on, although I was not always clear about the precise way in which the disciplines would come to be articulated. Something similar happened with my training in computing and data: I had the intuition that they could contribute to my work, but their place became clearer through concrete projects and problems. At each stage the objects, scales and research methods changed. There persisted, however, attention to the processes through which situated experiences and relationships acquire forms that allow them to be interpreted, organized and intervened, but also make them measurable, standardized, circulatable and governable.

  1. Psychology2018

    Psychologist and graduate in PsychologyUniversidad de La Serena

    ThesisMoral ethos of professional teacher training: possible meanings in first-year pedagogy students of the Universidad de La Serena.

    My initial training focused on educational processes and the interpretations that people make about their own experience. I participated in research on subjective theories, perception of teaching time and professional training, and I studied the moral meanings present in initial teacher training.

    Later I worked first as a school coexistence manager in a rural school and, later, as a community coordinator of school coexistence in the Municipality of Punitaqui. There these questions were found with rural schools, public regulations, administrative records and intersectoral coordination.

    That experience was one of the motivations to venture into other disciplines. I understood that intersectoral work required knowing the functioning and languages ​​of other organizations. When I recognized in the words of other actors concepts that I had tried to put into circulation, I found a concrete sign that we had begun to understand each other.

  2. Sociology2023

    Master in SociologyUniversidad Alberto Hurtado

    ThesisEmergence and evolution of school coexistence in Chile through national policy (2002–2019): the creation of an intervention domain and the assembly of a government tool.

    My motivation to study the master's degree arose from the daily interaction with regulatory documents during my work as a community coordinator. That experience shifted my attention from individual interpretations to public policies, organizations and government devices.

    I studied how relational and situated conflicts were transformed into standardized categories, protocols and indicators, capable of circulating and guiding interventions at a distance. The historical reconstruction made it possible to show that these forms of intervention did not appear all at once but rather acquired consistency through antecedents, disputes, reformulations and institutional projections.

    During this period I began to work more directly in academia, combining research and teaching in Psychology, Sociology and Differential Education. Between 2023 and August 2026 I participated in the creation and management of Centro de Intervención e Investigación en Psicología Educacional (CIPSE-UCEN), where I articulated research initiatives, links with the environment and production of pedagogical materials. Between 2025 and August 2026 I also accompanied the formulation, execution and writing of projects and bachelor's theses in Psychology.

  3. Anthropology2025–present

    PhD in Anthropology, in progressPontificia Universidad Católica de ChileCandidacy approved in July 2026

    doctoral thesisMaking life coherent: an ethnography in plant biotechnology laboratories in Chile.

    I am currently carrying out an ethnography on knowledge production in plant biotechnology. The research follows the relationships between plants, techniques, instruments, data, public institutions and companies, taking into account the different temporalities that converge in scientific work.

    The problem is no longer only how a social experience becomes governable, but how materially heterogeneous forms of life acquire coherence as scientific objects, information, and promises of intervention. Research moves these questions towards operations that reach molecular scales and towards the processes by which biological matter is transformed into comparable and circulatable information.

Additional training

I have completed complementary training in data, IT infrastructure, design, teaching and public management. These learnings expand the resources with which I can research, teach and build. Its specific application can be seen on the projects page.

Data and IT infrastructure

Data analysis and curation, databases, object-oriented programming, data networks and server administration.

Design and mediation

Customer experience, data and innovation, curatorship, consumer psychology, art and public space.

Teaching

Teaching for higher education, instructional design, self-regulation of learning, social-emotional learning and reading animation.

Management and public sector

Public management, territorial support for educational improvement, institutional use of data, probity and transparency.
